candidates.detail: GeneratedArmor exposes positions, joint_indices and joint_weights as independent public fields. Public skin_rules::attach checks the skin's rig-joint count against the names but not the number of skin rows against positions. For a solid helmet it looks up C_HEAD and calls fill over 0..positions.len(). fill first sets every joint-index row, then fills the weight slice. PackedRigSkin::set_vertex checks joint encoding but uses direct vector indexing. With two positions, one skin row, two weight rows, names [ROOT,C_HEAD] and a two-joint skin initially containing [0;8], the rig-bound guard and head lookup pass; row zero becomes [1;8] and row one indexes beyond the single row, causing an out-of-bounds panic before the weight slice is filled. This is source and array-bound reasoning; no armor, mutation, panic or product ran.
candidates.consumer_and_safeguards: device_fit::assemble_recipe constructs an armor record from a DevicePiece and skin then calls attach after textile material processing; selected studio and runtime parametric paths call assembly. This does not show that the normal device producers can return mismatched rows or that their earlier steps succeed for a malformed input. If a panic unwinds and a direct caller retains the object, earlier index rows may already have changed; behavior under abort profiles, actual malformed inputs and player impact are unestablished. Equal rig-joint counts establish ordinal bounds, not position/skin row correspondence.
